title: Adaptive throttle and kernel curation follow-up after heterogeneous-pool latency spike
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Post-incident follow-up for the 2025-11-17 latency spike affecting inference in the heterogeneous GPU pool. Multiple customers experienced P95/P99 tail latency regressions for long-context chat workloads; throughput dropped by 20-40% on affected shards. This ticket tracks immediate mitigations, engineering fixes, and long-term guardrails to prevent recurrence.
impact: Multiple paid tenants in dedicated and hosted tiers saw request timeouts and degraded SLAs between 2025-11-17 09:20 UTC and 2025-11-17 11:05 UTC. SLO alerts triggered and on-call engaged; some customers escalated to SEs. Total impacted requests estimated ~120k tokens affected across 6 tenant clusters.
timeline: 09:12 UTC - Autoscaler applied burst nodes to heterogeneous pool; 09:18 UTC - scheduler change 'prefer_low_mem_kernels' rolled for canary and then staged; 09:20 UTC - KV cache warmup rate dropped as new workers joined; 09:27 UTC - first SLO alert (p95 x2 baseline); 09:35-10:40 UTC - on-call throttled speculative recompile and applied traffic shaping; 11:05 UTC - traffic shaping and kernel-lock fallback fully rolled, latency returned near baseline.
root_cause: A recent scheduler heuristic intended to prioritize low-memory kernel variants interacted poorly with heterogeneous burst capacity. For long sequence lengths the low-memory variants had worse throughput and higher tail-latency due to less-efficient attention tiling. New workers joining during autoscale caused KV cache cold starts and increased quantization-variant probing. Combined, this produced kernel-choice churn and amplified per-request latency.
short_term_mitigations: Rolled back prefer_low_mem_kernels heuristic in production (09:40 UTC).
Enabled kernel_lock_fallback: pins in-flight requests to last-good kernel to prevent thrashing.
Applied traffic shaping to limit speculative recompile/probing rate per-shard for 30m windows.
Adjusted autoscaler ramp to add nodes with staggered warmup to preserve KV cache locality.
Communication: sent incident summary to impacted customers and opened SE tickets for high-touch customers.
medium_term_fixes: Introduce kernel-choice shadowing: run candidate kernel selection in parallel (sampling) to collect p95/p99 metrics before switching at scale.
Implement per-model adaptive throttle token bucket for speculative probing and recompile attempts (configurable by tenant).
Improve autoscaler warmup flow to prefetch KV cache headers and propagate warmup state across shards.
Add deterministic tie-break rules in scheduler that prefer historically stable kernels for tail-sensitive routes.
Create benchmark suite for long-context attention tiling across kernel variants (include quantized/non-quantized).
long_term_projects: Kernel quality scorecard: maintain per-kernel metrics (throughput, p50/p95/p99, memory, cold-warm delta) and expose in Console.
Model-serving canary pipeline: incrementally ramp new scheduler heuristics behind traffic % and automated rollback if tail metrics regress.
Cache-aware scheduling: extend scheduler to be cache-locality aware so that nodes with warm KV state are preferred for sequential tails.
Autoscaler rework: support staged node addition with KV warmup hooks and service-level capacity fences.

notes: Decision: do not remove kernel variants; instead harden the scheduler and rollout process. Avoid global heuristics that make optimistic assumptions about memory/tiling tradeoffs without empirical tail metrics.
postmortem_meeting: Scheduled 2025-11-22 16:00 UTC. Attendees: on-call, runtime leads, autoscaler, observability. Objective: agree owners and shipping milestones.
communication_plan: Customer-facing incident summary prepared and sent 2025-11-18. SEs assigned to high-impact tenants. Plan to publish public postmortem after mitigation verification and ticket closure.
resolution_criteria: Baseline tail latency returns to within 5% of pre-incident p95 for affected routes for 72h and kernel_mismatch_rate drops below 0.5% during canary windows.
risk_and_open_questions: 1) How often do autoscale join events coincide with high-concurrency tails in production? 2) Should we introduce a model-level safety label to opt out of speculative kernel probing? 3) How to balance kernel diversity for cost vs tail latency?
